- Keith directly asked Elizabeth whether he had done something to upset her.
- He heard Elizabeth say no, she was dealing with personal stuff, and she apologized if she seemed short. From this, he understood her shortness was not anger at him but personal stress.
- Keith felt sympathetic and wanted to support her. He offered to listen/talk and suggested a coffee break.
- He heard Elizabeth accept the coffee break and thank him.
- During coffee, Elizabeth shared more about her stresses; to Keith, they seemed severe. Keith suggested she consider talking to a professional, saying an external perspective can help. He heard her say she had thought about it but was unsure/hesitant about seeking help.
- Afterward, Keith observed Elizabeth become slightly withdrawn. He worried/regretted that his suggestion may have overstepped or embarrassed her.
- Keith told her he hoped he hadn’t overstepped and that he wanted her to know he was supportive no matter what. He heard her say he didn’t overstep, she appreciated his concern, and it was a lot to think about.
- Later, Keith observed Elizabeth seeming more open and appreciative. He believes she values his support and feels more comfortable around him. He intends to maintain this supportive relationship.
- Keith told her he was glad they talked and that he is always available if she needs to chat or take a break. He heard her thank him, say it means a lot, and that she feels better knowing she has his support.

Keith has no access to Elizabeth’s private thoughts or hidden events beyond what she said and what he observed in her behavior.
